hints.title: Capacity Feasibility Monotonicity
hints.text: Simulating package distribution over days works for any fixed vessel capacity. Since higher capacities always ship in fewer or equal days, how can you test the optimal capacity without checking every value?

hints.title: Feasibility Bound Invariant
hints.text: The minimum possible capacity is max(weights) because every package must fit, and the maximum is sum(weights). The condition feasible(cap) is monotonic from False to True.

hints.title: Answer Range Bisection Procedure
hints.text: Define feasible(cap): greedily accumulate package weights; whenever current sum exceeds cap, start a new day. If required days <= days, cap is feasible. Bisect over [max(weights), sum(weights)]. When feasible(mid) is true, shrink right = mid; otherwise left = mid + 1. Return left.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Logarithmic bisection on monotonic capacity range running linear greedy validation each probe.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing every capacity from max(weights) to sum(weights) sequentially takes O(N * sum(weights)) which times out.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy linear checks require zero auxiliary storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Justifying lower bound max(weights) and upper bound sum(weights) and explaining greedy partition optimality.
